introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.corrige_markdown:
The denominator has two distinct linear factors and the numerator has lower degree, so write

$$\frac{4x+3}{(2x-1)(3x+1)} \equiv \frac{A}{2x-1} + \frac{B}{3x+1}.$$

Multiply through by $(2x-1)(3x+1)$:

$$4x + 3 \equiv A(3x+1) + B(2x-1).$$

Substitute $x = \dfrac12$ (this kills the $B$ term): $4\cdot\dfrac12 + 3 = 5 = A\left(\dfrac32 + 1\right) = \dfrac52 A$, so $A = 2$.

Substitute $x = -\dfrac13$ (this kills the $A$ term): $4\left(-\dfrac13\right) + 3 = \dfrac53 = B\left(-\dfrac23 - 1\right) = -\dfrac53 B$, so $B = -1$.

$$\boxed{\frac{4x+3}{(2x-1)(3x+1)} = \frac{2}{2x-1} - \frac{1}{3x+1}}$$

Check by recombining: $\dfrac{2(3x+1) - (2x-1)}{(2x-1)(3x+1)} = \dfrac{4x+3}{(2x-1)(3x+1)}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the roots of the quadratic equation $x^2 + (k+1)x + k = 0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$, find the values of the real constant $k$ for which $\alpha = 2\beta$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $x^2 + (k+1)x + k = 0$ the sum and product of the roots are

$$\alpha + \beta = -(k+1), \qquad \alpha\beta = k.$$

Put $\alpha = 2\beta$:

$$3\beta = -(k+1) \;\Longrightarrow\; \beta = -\frac{k+1}{3}, \qquad 2\beta^2 = k.$$

Substitute $\beta$ into the product equation:

$$2\cdot\frac{(k+1)^2}{9} = k \;\Longrightarrow\; 2(k+1)^2 = 9k \;\Longrightarrow\; 2k^2 - 5k + 2 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; (2k-1)(k-2) = 0.$$

$$\boxed{k = \tfrac12 \quad\text{or}\quad k = 2}$$

Check. For $k = 2$: $x^2 + 3x + 2 = (x+1)(x+2)$, roots $-1$ and $-2$, and $-2 = 2(-1)$, so $\alpha = -2$, $\beta = -1$ works. For $k = \tfrac12$: $x^2 + \tfrac32 x + \tfrac12 = (x+1)\left(x+\tfrac12\right)$, roots $-1$ and $-\tfrac12$, and $-1 = 2\left(-\tfrac12\right)$, so $\alpha = -1$, $\beta = -\tfrac12$ works. In both cases the roots are real, as required.
